title: eROSITA X-ray data show that many TESS main-sequence M dwarfs with periods below 0.3 d are not saturated fast rotators, which removes about half of the main-sequence CPV deficit
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. An earlier result found that main-sequence M dwarfs at the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x of young CPV hosts have 2 CPVs where the contraction (x-only) model predicts 8.9. To reach that x, a main-sequence star must rotate in P < 0.3 d, and its corona must then be saturated (log Lx/Lbol near -3.2). We used eRASS1 (eROSITA-DE DR1) aperture photometry for all 41,046 TESS 2-minute red dwarfs of the CPV samples in the eROSITA-DE sky, with a censored Poisson model that includes non-detections. The X-ray-saturated fraction of the rapid rotators is 0.97 for 1-24 Myr members, 0.99 for 35-750 Myr members, but 0.82 (0.78-0.86) for main-sequence stars, and 0.34 (0.10-0.65) for main-sequence stars with P < 0.2 d. Most non-saturated stars have a bright or co-moving Gaia neighbour within 40 arcsec, so their TESS period probably belongs to another star. When we weight each star by its probability to be a saturated rotator, the frozen x-only model predicts 4.4 (2.3-7.2) main-sequence CPVs for 2 observed (p = 0.22), against 8.5 (p = 0.015) without weights. Variants give 4.0-4.8 (p = 0.18-0.28). Neighbour-clean main-sequence stars still have 0 CPVs for 2.5 predicted (p = 0.11), so a smaller second age effect remains possible. CPV hosts have normal saturated coronae: at fixed x their log Lx/Lbol differs by -0.05 +/- 0.10 dex from other rapid rotators. In neighbour-clean stars the coronal level does not depend on P, but falls by 0.1-0.2 dex at small x (p = 0.001-0.02), as centrifugal stripping predicts in direction. Limitations: half of the sky has X-ray data; one X-ray epoch; small cells at short periods; we did not inspect TESS pixels to confirm the period source.

(a) Stars without a bright (G < G*+1) or co-moving (parallax > 3 mas) Gaia neighbour within 40 arcsec. (b) Stars with such a neighbour. All-sky test of the frozen x-only CPV model of sci:sha256:b46f8555 in main-sequence rapid rotators. Grey: prediction for all TESS rapid rotators. Black diamonds: observed CPVs (open = 0). Bars are 95% bootstrap intervals. The 35-750 Myr row is a check.

Bars are standard errors.

citations.reason: We repeat its frozen x-only main-sequence CPV test and show that about half of its predicted main-sequence CPVs come from rapid rotators that are not X-ray saturated; the deficit becomes non-significant (p 0.015 to 0.18-0.28). We reuse its S1-S55 periods, labels, efficiencies and code.
We reuse its stellar-parameter code and x-only rate model; with X-ray-confirmed rotators its contraction model is consistent with the main-sequence CPV count.
